Title: January 8, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting

Topic1.Title: Agenda Amendment and Open Comment
Topic1.Summary: Council unanimously amended the agenda to add a report on the city's response to the public safety power shutoff and windstorms, and removed an item on sending a letter to Xcel Energy, which will return January 22. Open comment included over a dozen speakers on topics such as surface parking, Flock Safety surveillance concerns, eco visits for CU students, Xcel Energy, proportional representation, Caterpillar divestment, and recreation center plans. City staff responded to questions on community resilience hubs, closed captioning, and data protection policy for Flock. The public comment period closed at 6:12 p.m. before the meeting recessed.

Topic2.Title: Public Safety Power Shutoff and Windstorm Response Report
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented a summary of the city's response to the December public safety power shutoff and high wind event, noting that about 60% of the community lost power. Fire, police, utilities, parks, housing, and other departments reported extensive activations, including an emergency operations center, extended police shifts, and closure of the open space system. Staff will hold a virtual community town hall later this month and conduct an after-action review to improve future responses. Council members thanked staff for their work and encouraged questions to be directed to staff.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda and Downtown Commercial District Resolution on Sundance Institute
Topic3.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda items 4A through 4C and 4E through 4K unanimously, with item 4D removed earlier. Council then convened as the Downtown Commercial District Board of Directors and unanimously approved Resolution 319 approving incentives and authorizing a lease with the Sundance Institute to host the Sundance Film Festival from 2027 through 2036. Revenue sharing on up to 1,000 parking spaces during the festival was discussed, along with calls for annual reporting and an equity analysis.

Topic4.Title: Call-Up of 5501 and 5505 Arapahoe Avenue Form-Based Code Review
Topic4.Summary: Council considered calling up a form-based code review for a five-story mixed-use building with 300 dwelling units at 5501 and 5505 Arapahoe Avenue. Some members expressed concern about the building's aesthetics and the planning board's divided recommendation. Others argued the project followed the adopted code and that code changes, not a call-up, should address design concerns. The motion to call up the project failed on a 4-5 vote.

Topic5.Title: Nwood Metropolitan District 2025 Budget Amendment
Topic5.Summary: Council, acting as the Nwood Metropolitan District Board of Directors, reviewed a supplemental appropriation of about $7,400 to cover dissolution-related expenses that exceeded the original 2025 budget. Staff noted an accounting error in the prior year that will result in a temporary negative fund balance. One public commenter raised concerns about costs during a budget crisis. Resolution 4 was adopted unanimously.

Topic6.Title: 915 Fifth Street Annexation and Zoning
Topic6.Summary: Council held the second reading and public hearing on the series annexation of 915 Fifth Street, a 1.294-acre property with initial residential estate zoning. The planning board had recommended limiting floor area to 4,000 square feet, but staff recommended against this, finding existing zoning standards sufficient. No public comment was received on the item. Council unanimously adopted Resolutions 1364 and 1365 and Ordinances 8728, 8729, and 8730, approving the annexation and inclusion in the Northern Colorado Water Conservancy District.

Topic7.Title: Wildfire Hardening and Water-Wise Landscaping Ordinance
Topic7.Summary: Council held a continued second reading of Ordinance 8721, which updates landscaping, water conservation, and wildfire resilience standards and moves technical requirements into an administrative landscape manual. Staff revised the proposal to remove tree removal requirements, add limbing-up standards, and ease several restrictions in response to council feedback. Council members praised the flexibility and the staff work, and recommended that the city lead by example on city-owned properties. Ordinance 8721 was amended and approved, with third reading scheduled for February.

Topic8.Title: 2026 Council Committee Appointments
Topic8.Summary: Council discussed filling vacancies on boards, committees, and sister city liaison positions for 2026. Members volunteered for roles including the Boulder County Consortium of Cities, Mile High Flood District, Charter Committee, Financial Strategy Committee, Intergovernmental Affairs, and several sister city liaison roles. Staff will look into the homelessness working group appointment and whether the Resource Conservation Advisory Board appointment could become a staff appointment. Members were asked to submit additional recommendations by January 13.
